solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Curse man's choice of words

parts.note: man's, as in belonging to a man, is the adjective male
diction is a speaker's or writer's choice of words

explanation.surface: A man's foul language is itself a kind of curse.
explanation.definitionFit: A malediction is a spoken curse, the opposite of a benediction or blessing.

clue.text: Middle-aged woman left, pursuing journalists

indicators.note: pursuing means the woman and left come after the journalists

parts.note: the media are journalists collectively
Eva is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A middle-aged woman leaves, chased by the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle-aged' looks like a description of the woman but means of the Middle Ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediaeval means belonging to the Middle Ages, which is a playful reading of middle-aged.

clue.text: Nearly neglected to arrest leader of criminals for rustling, say

indicators.note: to arrest means to hold, so the scrambled letters hold the next piece
neglected suggests the word is left in disarray, so its letters are rearranged
leader of means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Police almost failed to catch the ringleader of cattle thieves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neglected' rearranges NEARLY to LARENY, and 'to arrest' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustling is the theft of livestock, so it is one example of the crime of theft.

clue.text: Word from Richard's girl

parts.note: Dicky is a pet form of Richard, so Richard's girl is Dicky's girl
bird is British slang for a girl

explanation.surface: A message passed on from Richard's girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky bird' is British rhyming slang for word, as in 'not a dicky bird'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dicky bird is rhyming slang meaning a word, used in phrases like not saying a single one.

clue.text: Stand-up's initiation of laughter for minutes causes gripes

indicators.note: for signals that one letter takes the place of the other

parts.note: a stand-up is a comic, a comedian who performs standing alone

indicators.note: initiation of means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A comedian's opening laugh lines take minutes and set off complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps L, the first letter of laughter, in place of M in COMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Gripes are sharp stomach pains, which is what colic is.

clue.text: Popular former performance not accurate

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
ex means former, as in ex-wife
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: A review says a well-loved old show was not faithful to the original.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexact means lacking precision, so it is a synonym of imprecise or wrong.

clue.text: Havers, perhaps missing the Spanish height in the dark

indicators.note: missing means the following word's letters are dropped

parts.note: Nigel Havers is an English actor, so Havers is an example of a Nigel
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish-speaking actor missing in the dark, measured for height.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the time of darkness, so it is a synonym of the dark.

clue.text: Tree that's been around for longer

definitions.meaning: a shrub or small tree with white flowers and dark berries
older, having lived for more years than another

explanation.definitionFit: Elder names the tree and also means older, the senior of two people.

clue.text: Record one rushing to grab policeman in a right reverend manner

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: to grab means the first word takes hold of the second

parts.note: a sally is a sudden rush forward, a sortie
cop is slang for a policeman

explanation.surface: Someone on record says a person ran to seize a policeman, very reverently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right Reverend' is the formal title of a bishop, which is why it points to bishops.
explanation.definitionFit: Episcopally means in the manner of bishops, and Right Reverend is a bishop's formal title.

clue.text: After depression, distance associate

indicators.note: the distance word is placed after the depression word in the answer

parts.note: a col is a dip or pass between two mountain peaks
a league is an old measure of distance, about three miles

explanation.surface: After a bout of depression, someone distances themselves from a person they work with.
explanation.definitionFit: A colleague is a fellow worker, someone you are associated with professionally.

clue.text: Doubter upset soccer tie-up

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sceptic is unhappy about a football partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: A Eurosceptic doubts the benefits of the European Union, a specific kind of doubter.

clue.text: Dream I am long time on railway

parts.note: contracted to I'm
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: Someone daydreams about spending ages on a train.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagery is pictures formed in the mind, so a dream or vision counts as a loose synonym.

clue.text: Idle talk about milliner

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
a hatter makes and sells hats, as a milliner does

explanation.surface: Gossip doing the rounds about a hat-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatter is trivial, rapid conversation, which is exactly idle talk.

clue.text: Small party where chap's unknown

parts.note: read as chap is; a cove is old British slang for a chap or fellow
Y is one of the algebraic unknowns, along with X and Z

explanation.surface: A little gathering where a certain fellow is a stranger to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A covey is a small flock of game birds, and by extension a small group of people.

clue.text: Busy Lizzie possibly intolerant, short with son

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: impatient, unwilling to put up with delay or others
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A woman nicknamed Busy Lizzie is perhaps short-tempered with her boy.
explanation.walkthrough: Busy Lizzie reads like a person's nickname, but it is the common name of a garden flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Impatiens is the plant genus that includes the busy Lizzie, so the flower is one example of it.

clue.text: These boxes could be happy ones

indicators.note: could be says the letters may be arranged into another form

explanation.surface: A cheerful remark that some boxes might be happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' suggests containers, but these are telephone kiosks.
explanation.definitionFit: Payphones are coin telephones housed in kiosks, often called phone boxes in Britain.

clue.text: River flows round about level and clear

indicators.note: flows round means the river is placed around the next piece

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England
on means about, as in a talk on a subject
a rate is a level or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A river runs around a level stretch and comes out clear.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate someone is to clear them of blame or guilt.

clue.text: Girl's heartless, a new right-winger, in practice of having several husbands

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the name is taken out

parts.note: Polly is a girl's name; the 's is read as is
a dry is a hardline right-wing Conservative in British politics

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted girl, newly turned right-wing, takes several husbands.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics a 'dry' was a Thatcherite hardliner, as against the moderate 'wets'.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyandry is the custom of a woman having more than one husband at a time.

clue.text: Under review, Fat Tom's sternest

indicators.note: under review means being reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An overweight man called Tom is being judged at his most severe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sternest' looks like most severe, but it means nearest the stern of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Aftmost means furthest aft, the nautical position nearest the back, or stern.

clue.text: Distressed heron in river

indicators.note: distressed means agitated or knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An upset wading bird is seen standing in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhone is a major European river flowing from Switzerland through France.

clue.text: Wine found in upturned container with lid off

indicators.note: upturned in a down clue means the letters read from bottom to top
with lid off means the top, or first, letter is removed

parts.note: a canister is a metal container

explanation.surface: Wine is found in a tin turned upside down without its lid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with lid off' removes C from CANISTER, leaving ANISTER, and 'upturned' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Girl allowed sex appeal to come before intellectual activity initially

indicators.note: the earlier pieces are placed ahead of the initials that follow

parts.note: let means permitted or allowed
it is old slang for sex appeal, as in the 'It girl'

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of the two words are used

explanation.surface: A girl was permitted to let her allure take priority over thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Letitia is a female first name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Mosaic creator's a half-hearted farmer

definitions.note: the 's reads as is, so the definition is the mosaic creator

indicators.note: half-hearted means half of the central double letter is removed

parts.note: a tiller is someone who tills the soil, a farmer

explanation.surface: An artist who makes mosaics is only a half-committed farmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiler lays tiles, and mosaics are made by setting small tiles.

clue.text: Terrible, not beginning to be legitimate

indicators.note: not beginning means the first letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: lawful means legitimate, allowed by law

explanation.surface: Something dreadful is not even close to being legal.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful means very bad or dreadful, a synonym of terrible.

clue.text: Superlatively passionate, he's taking too much time

indicators.note: taking means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: taken as the letters of he's without the apostrophe
OTT is short for over the top, meaning too much

explanation.surface: A very ardent man is spending too long over something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superlatively' signals the -est form; OTT, short for over the top, is common crossword slang for too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Hottest is the superlative form of hot, meaning most passionate or ardent.

clue.text: Shout cry of pain, with half of finger taken away in big fish

parts.note: to yell is to shout
ow is what someone cries when hurt

indicators.note: half of means only the front half of the word finger is kept
taken away says the back half of the word finger is removed, leaving only its front

explanation.surface: Someone yells in agony after losing half a finger to a large fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken away' only reinforces 'half of': the rest of finger is lost, leaving its first half.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellowfin is a large tuna, a big game fish of warm seas.

clue.text: Newton, maybe, is measure of current that's current?

parts.note: A is the symbol for the ampere, the unit of electric current
AC stands for alternating current

explanation.surface: A puzzle about whether a unit of current is itself current, or up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newton' looks like the unit of force alongside the current units, but it is Sir Isaac Newton.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac was the first name of the physicist Newton, so Newton is one example of an Isaac.

clue.text: Vigorous eternal task for American viper

indicators.note: vigorous means energetically shaken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An endless, energetic job of dealing with a snake in America.
explanation.definitionFit: The rattlesnake is a venomous pit viper of the Americas with a rattle on its tail.
